title: Miss Gloria's Extension Cord
subject: a block party whose DJ keeps losing power because the extension cord runs through Miss Gloria's kitchen
caption: New Orleans bounce on the Triggerman beat. Booming 808 kicks; rapid TR-808 handclap rolls; the Triggerman bell riff looping every bar; a short stabbed synth bass on the one; a crowd of shouting voices answering the lead lines. Heavy and dry, the low end huge and forward, almost no harmony, the arrangement repeating hard. Female voice, a commanding block-party MC, shouting and chanting with high energy in call-and-response with the crowd. 102 BPM, G minor. Rowdy, bossy and laughing. No trap hi-hat rolls, no sung pop chorus, no Baltimore club breakbeat, no autotune, no smooth R&B.
lyrics:
[Intro - Triggerman bell riff and 808 clap roll]

[Verse 1]
St. Claude and Music, Saturday, tables in the street
DJ Trey got the speakers stacked up six high
All the power coming down one orange cord
Through Miss Gloria's window, past her stove, to the plug by her fridge

[Hook]
Who got the power? (Miss Gloria!)
Who got the power? (Miss Gloria!)
She's cooking gumbo and she needs that outlet
Who got the power? (Miss Gloria!)

[Verse 2]
Every time she plugs the rice cooker in, the whole block goes dark
Thirty people freeze in the middle of a bounce
DJ Trey on his knees at her screen door, begging
She say "baby, you can have it when the rice is done"

[Bridge - claps only, crowd answers]
Rice is done! (Rice is done!)
Now take it to the ground! (To the ground!)

[Hook]
Who got the power? (Miss Gloria!)
Who got the power? (Miss Gloria!)
She's on the porch with a ladle and a cash box
First bowl five, and the plug's included! (Miss Gloria!)

[Outro - bell riff, kick drops out]
Second bowl, two dollars
And the plug stay hers
